title: Cameras and Scrolling Worlds
summary: A world bigger than the screen needs a camera. This lesson uses raylib's Camera2D - target, offset, zoom and rotation - converts between screen and world coordinates, and makes the camera follow the player smoothly with a dead zone, look-ahead, limits at the level's edges and screen shake.

cards.q: What do a Camera2D's target and offset mean?
cards.a: The target is the world point the camera looks at; the offset is where on the screen that point is drawn.

cards.q: How do you find which world point the mouse is over?
What is a camera dead zone?
cards.a: A box around the screen's centre within which the player can move without the camera moving.
